extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and writers interested in folktale/narrative structure (Proppian analysis)
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Vladimir Propp's Morphology of the Folktale to identify functions and actant roles in wonder-tales (fairy tales), using the canonical set of 31 functions and seven character roles as analytic units. Useful for literary analysis, storytelling, and media narrative design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of the hero's community or family leaves the security of the home environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be the hero himself or another relation the hero must later rescue; injects initial tension and often serves as the hero's introduction, portraying him as an ordinary person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A forbidding edict or command is passed upon the hero ('don't go there', 'don't do this').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero is warned against some action; sets up a rule that frames subsequent violation and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of interdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior rule is violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether accidental or intentional, violation typically leads to negative consequences; often introduces the villain into the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconnaissance
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain makes an effort to attain knowledge needed to fulfil his plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often involves disguises, probing for information from innocents, or seeking out the hero to gauge strengths and special nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain succeeds at recon and gains a lead on his intended victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May involve a map or acquired information that advances the villain's plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trickery
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain attempts to deceive the victim to acquire something valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include conning protagonists, ransoming valuables, or otherwise manipulating trust to gain access or resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complicity
rubrics_metrics.description: The victim is fooled or forced to concede and unwittingly or unwillingly helps the villain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants the villain access to previously off-limits places (e.g., the hero's home or a vault) and advances the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Villainy or lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain harms a family member or a protagonist finds something lacking in the home environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers harms such as abduction, theft, plundering, banishment, murder, or the imposition of lacks (need for potion, artifact); villain may be indirect or manipulative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediation
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more of the negative factors comes to the attention of the Hero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero uncovers deceit, perceives the lack, or learns of the villain's acts; this catalyses the hero's involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginning counteraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero considers ways to resolve the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hero plans to seek a magical item, rescue captives, or otherwise thwart the villain; a defining initiation of heroic agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departure
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero leaves the home environment with a sense of purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks the formal start of the adventure or quest.

rubrics_metrics.name: First function of the donor
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero encounters a magical agent or helper (donor) and is tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests can be interrogation, combat, puzzles, or other trials that prepare the hero or assess worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero's reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero responds to the actions of his future donor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses may include withstanding tests, freeing captives, reconciling parties, or otherwise performing good services that reveal character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of a magical agent
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero acquires use of a magical agent as a consequence of his actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magical agent can be an item, summoned aid, consumed magical food, loyalty of another, or an object found/earned/fashioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is transferred, delivered or led to a vital location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May relate to donor's home, location of the magical agent or parts, or the villain's lair; often facilitated by helpers or the agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero and villain meet and engage in conflict directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict can be battle, contest, or another form of direct confrontation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is marked in some manner (scar, ring, scarf, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking may identify the hero later and is often a token tied to recognition; can result from trials or combat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Victory
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain is defeated by the hero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defeat may be killing, out-performing in contest, banishment, or exploiting a vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier misfortunes or issues of the story are resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objects of search are distributed, spells broken, captives freed; the balance is restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero travels back to his home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks the conclusion of the journey phase before final resolution or recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is pursued by a threatening adversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pursuer seeks capture or harm; pursuit often generates further obstacles for the hero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescue
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is saved from a chase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescue may be by obstacles that delay the pursuer, hiding, transformation, or aid of another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrecognized arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero arrives and is unrecognised or unacknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrival can be at destination or along journey; sets stage for testing, false claims, or recognition scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfounded claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A false hero presents unfounded claims or deceits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False hero may be villain, underling, or unrelated party who takes credit or makes false claims to reward or marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficult task
rubrics_metrics.description: A trial is proposed to the hero (riddles, strength tests, acrobatics, ordeals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trials test hero's abilities and often precede solution and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero accomplishes a difficult task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achievement of task often proves hero's worth and leads to reward/recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is given due recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition is usually by means of prior branding or token and leads toward final settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: The false hero and/or villain is exposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deceit or false claims are revealed publicly, clearing the way for just rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfiguration
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero gains a new appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can reflect aging, recovery, or magical restoration—serves to improve status or indicate transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The villain suffers the consequences of his actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishment may be enacted by the hero, avenged victims, or through the villain's own devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedding
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero marries and is rewarded or promoted by the family or community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often the final function: hero ascends socially (e.g., to a throne) and order is restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propp's 31 functions (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on analysis of 100 folktales, Propp identifies 31 basic structural elements (functions) that typically occur within Russian fairy tales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions occur in a specific, fixed ascending order (1–31) though not every tale contains every function; a tale is composed of a selection of these functions in that order. This syntagmatic focus emphasizes event sequence rather than paradigmatic oppositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function inversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Some functions may be inverted (occur in different positions or with reversed effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the hero receives an artifact while still at home, fulfilling the donor function early; inversions alter canonical ordering but are recognized within Proppian analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition/threefold pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical function repetition pattern in Western tales: functions are often negated twice and thus repeated three times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propp notes conventional repetition (rule of three) as a cultural tendency in Western folktales; analysts should look for episodic triads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven character (actant) functions
rubrics_metrics.description: All characters can be resolved into seven abstract character functions: villain, dispatcher, helper, princess (or prize) and often her father, donor, hero, and false hero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles are abstract (actants) and can be distributed across multiple characters or combined in one character; use these categories to map social/functional roles rather than specific persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: The villain
rubrics_metrics.description: An evil character that creates struggles for the hero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May act directly or indirectly; instigates harmful events and lacks morale; central source of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: The dispatcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Any character who illustrates the need for the hero's quest and sends the hero off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often overlaps with princess's father; acts to motivate or authorize the quest.

rubrics_metrics.name: The helper
rubrics_metrics.description: A typically magical entity that comes to help the hero in their quest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance, magical agents, or direct assistance in overcoming trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: The princess or prize (and often her father)
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the quest to which the hero aspires; the hero deserves her but is prevented by evil or injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marriage to the princess often concludes the hero's journey and signifies social elevation and villain's defeat.

rubrics_metrics.name: The donor
rubrics_metrics.description: A character that prepares the hero or gives the hero some magical object, sometimes after testing them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donor's test and gift are crucial for the hero's acquisition of helpful agency; donor functions may be combined with other roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: The hero
rubrics_metrics.description: The character who reacts to the dispatcher and donor, thwarts the villain, resolves lacks and weds the princess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central protagonist whose actions and reactions constitute the story's moral and structural progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: The false hero
rubrics_metrics.description: A Miles Gloriosus figure who takes credit for the hero's actions or tries to marry the princess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be exposed and punished; provides contrast and testing for authentic recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntagmatic methodological orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Propp's analysis is syntagmatic: it focuses on the events of a story and the order in which they occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with paradigmatic (Lévi-Strauss) approaches that seek underlying binary oppositions; use Propp when event sequence and functional ordering are primary analytic concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain limitation: wonder-tale/fairy tale specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Propp applied his morphology specifically to the wonder tale (fairy tale or skazka) within Russian folklore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While Propp's model has been applied more widely (literature, film, games), the canonical 31 functions were derived from Russian wonder-tales and may not map perfectly onto other narratives or genres.
